sanskrit: āghrāya rāmas taṃ mūrdhni pariṣvajya ca rāghavaḥ aṅke bharatam āropya paryapṛcchat samāhitaḥ
english: Rāma the Rāghava, having smelt him on the crown of his head and embraced him, placed Bharata on his lap and then, composed, began to question him.

sanskrit: kva nu te 'bhūt pitā tāta yad araṇyaṃ tvam āgataḥ na hi tvaṃ jīvatas tasya vanam āgantum arhasi
english: "Where then was your father, dear boy, that you have come to the forest? For as long as he lives, you have no right to come to the forest."

sanskrit: cirasya bata paśyāmi dūrād bharatam āgatam duṣpratīkam araṇye 'smin kiṃ tāta vanam āgataḥ
english: "Alas, after a long time I see Bharata arrived from afar, bearing a grim aspect here in this forest — why, dear boy, have you come to the forest?"

sanskrit: kaccid daśaratho rājā kuśalī satyasaṃgaraḥ rājasūyāśvamedhānām āhartā dharmaniścayaḥ
english: "Is King Daśaratha well — he of firm vows, performer of Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices, resolute in righteousness?"

sanskrit: sa kaccid brāhmaṇo vidvān dharmanityo mahādyutiḥ ikṣvākūṇām upādhyāyo yathāvat tāta pūjyate
english: "Is that learned brahmin, ever devoted to dharma, of great splendour, the preceptor of the Ikṣvākus — is he still duly honoured, dear boy?"

sanskrit: tāta kaccic ca kausalyā sumitrā ca prajāvatī sukhinī kaccid āryā ca devī nandati kaikayī
english: "Dear boy, is Kausalyā well, and Sumitrā the mother of good children — is the noble queen Kaikeyī also happy?"

sanskrit: kaccid vinaya saṃpannaḥ kulaputro bahuśrutaḥ anasūyur anudraṣṭā satkṛtas te purohitaḥ
english: "Is your family priest — a son of noble lineage, endowed with humility, widely learned, free from envy, a supervisor rather than a critic — duly honoured?"

sanskrit: kaccid agniṣu te yukto vidhijño matimān ṛjuḥ hutaṃ ca hoṣyamāṇaṃ ca kāle vedayate sadā
english: "Is there one assigned to your sacred fires who knows the prescribed rites, is intelligent and upright, and always informs you in good time of what has been offered and what is yet to be offered?"

sanskrit: iṣvastravarasaṃpannam arthaśāstraviśāradam sudhanvānam upādhyāyaṃ kaccit tvaṃ tāta manyase
english: "Do you honour Sudhanvan as your instructor, dear boy — he who is endowed with excellent mastery of the bow and weapons and is learned in the science of polity?"

sanskrit: kaccid ātma samāḥ śūrāḥ śrutavanto jitendriyāḥ kulīnāś ceṅgitajñāś ca kṛtās te tāta mantriṇaḥ
english: "Have you appointed as your ministers, dear boy, those who are your equals in spirit, who are brave, learned, with senses mastered, of noble birth, and skilled in reading signs and gestures?"

sanskrit: mantro vijayamūlaṃ hi rājñāṃ bhavati rāghava susaṃvṛto mantradharair amātyaiḥ śāstrakovidaiḥ
english: "For counsel is the root of victory for kings, O Rāghava, when it is well guarded by ministers who are keepers of secrets and versed in the śāstras."

sanskrit: kaccin nidrāvaśaṃ naiṣi kaccit kāle vibudhyase kac ciṃś cāpararātriṣu cintayasy arthanaipuṇam
english: "Do you not fall under the sway of sleep? Do you wake at the proper time? Do you, in the latter portions of the night, reflect on matters requiring skillful management?"

sanskrit: kaccin mantrayase naikaḥ kaccin na bahubhiḥ saha kaccit te mantrito mantro rāṣṭraṃ na paridhāvati
english: "Do you deliberate not alone, yet also not with too many? Does the counsel you have deliberated not run loose throughout the kingdom?"

sanskrit: kaccid arthaṃ viniścitya laghumūlaṃ mahodayam kṣipram ārabhase kartuṃ na dīrghayasi rāghava
english: "Having determined upon a course of action whose foundation is light but whose fruit is great, do you promptly set about executing it, without delay, O Rāghava?"

sanskrit: kaccit tu sukṛtāny eva kṛtarūpāṇi vā punaḥ vidus te sarvakāryāṇi na kartavyāni pārthivāḥ
english: "Do only those who have done well — or at least those who have given the semblance of doing well — know all your affairs that are not to be transacted?"

sanskrit: kaccin na tarkair yuktvā vā ye cāpy aparikīrtitāḥ tvayā vā tava vāmātyair budhyate tāta mantritam
english: "Is the counsel deliberated by you or by your ministers not inferred by those who are unnamed, through logic or other means, dear boy?"

sanskrit: kaccit sahasrān mūrkhāṇām ekam icchasi paṇḍitam paṇḍito hy arthakṛcchreṣu kuryān niḥśreyasaṃ mahat
english: "Do you desire one wise man over a thousand fools? For a wise man in difficult situations can bring about the highest good."

sanskrit: sahasrāṇy api mūrkhāṇāṃ yady upāste mahīpatiḥ atha vāpy ayutāny eva nāsti teṣu sahāyatā
english: "Even if a king keeps thousands or indeed tens of thousands of fools in attendance, there is no help to be had from them."

sanskrit: eko 'py amātyo medhāvī śūro dakṣo vicakṣaṇaḥ rājānaṃ rājamātraṃ vā prāpayen mahatīṃ śriyam
english: "Even a single minister who is intelligent, brave, capable, and discerning can bring a king — or even one who is king in name only — to great prosperity."

sanskrit: kaccin mukhyā mahatsv eva madhyameṣu ca madhyamāḥ jaghanyāś ca jaghanyeṣu bhṛtyāḥ karmasu yojitāḥ
english: "Are your servants employed in tasks befitting their grade — the foremost in foremost duties, the middling in middling ones, and the lowest in the lowest?"

sanskrit: amātyān upadhātītān pitṛpaitāmahāñ śucīn śreṣṭhāñ śreṣṭheṣu kaccit tvaṃ niyojayasi karmasu
english: "Do you appoint to the highest offices those ministers who have been tested by the fourfold temptations, who served your father and grandfather, who are pure, and who are the best?"

sanskrit: kaccit tvāṃ nāvajānanti yājakāḥ patitaṃ yathā ugrapratigrahītāraṃ kāmayānam iva striyaḥ
english: "Do officiating priests not disregard you as they would a fallen man, as women disdain one greedy to receive gifts and driven by desire?"

sanskrit: upāyakuśalaṃ vaidyaṃ bhṛtyasaṃdūṣaṇe ratam śūram aiśvaryakāmaṃ ca yo na hanti sa vadhyate
english: "A physician skilled in stratagem, one devoted to corrupting servants, and a brave man hungry for dominion — he who does not slay these three deserves to be slain."

sanskrit: kaccid dhṛṣṭaś ca śūraś ca dhṛtimān matimāñ śuciḥ kulīnaś cānuraktaś ca dakṣaḥ senāpatiḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "Have you appointed as your commander a man who is bold and brave, steadfast, wise, pure, of noble birth, loyal, and capable?"

sanskrit: balavantaś ca kaccit te mukhyā yuddhaviśāradāḥ dṛṣṭāpadānā vikrāntās tvayā satkṛtya mānitāḥ
english: "Are your principal warriors — powerful, skilled in battle, whose deeds have been witnessed, and of proven valour — honoured and esteemed by you?"

sanskrit: ka cid balasya bhaktaṃ ca vetanaṃ ca yathocitam saṃprāptakālaṃ dātavyaṃ dadāsi na vilambase
english: "Do you give your army their rations and pay, proper and befitting, when the time comes due, without delay?"

sanskrit: kālātikramaṇe hy eva bhakta vetanayor bhṛtāḥ bhartuḥ kupyanti duṣyanti so 'narthaḥ sumahān smṛtaḥ
english: "For when the time for rations and pay is overstepped, retainers grow angry at their master and become corrupted — this is reckoned a very great calamity."

sanskrit: kaccit sarve 'nuraktās tvāṃ kulaputrāḥ pradhānataḥ kaccit prāṇāṃs tavārtheṣu saṃtyajanti samāhitāḥ
english: "Are all your principal men of noble birth devoted to you? Are they resolved to lay down their lives in your cause?"

sanskrit: kaccij jānapado vidvān dakṣiṇaḥ pratibhānavān yathoktavādī dūtas te kṛto bharata paṇḍitaḥ
english: "Have you appointed as your envoy, O Bharata, one who is learned in the ways of the country, astute, resourceful, who speaks according to instruction, and is a man of wisdom?"

sanskrit: kaccid aṣṭādaśāny eṣu svapakṣe daśa pañca ca tribhis tribhir avijñātair vetsi tīrthāni cārakaiḥ
english: "Do you know by spies, in threes, undetected, the eighteen vulnerable points in the enemy's realm, and the fifteen in your own?"

sanskrit: kaccid vyapāstān ahitān pratiyātāṃś ca sarvadā durbalān anavajñāya vartase ripusūdana
english: "Do you always deal firmly with enemies who have been expelled and who have returned, without despising them as weak, O slayer of foes?"

sanskrit: kaccin na lokāyatikān brāhmaṇāṃs tāta sevase anartha kuśalā hy ete bālāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ
english: "Do you not frequent, dear boy, those brāhmaṇas who follow materialist philosophy? For these are childish men, skilled only in mischief, who fancy themselves wise."

sanskrit: dharmaśāstreṣu mukhyeṣu vidyamāneṣu durbudhāḥ buddhimān vīkṣikīṃ prāpya nirarthaṃ pravadanti te
english: "Though the foremost scriptures of dharma exist, these dull-witted men, having gotten hold of logic, speak fruitless words."

sanskrit: vīrair adhyuṣitāṃ pūrvam asmākaṃ tāta pūrvakaiḥ satyanāmāṃ dṛḍhadvārāṃ hastyaśvarathasaṃkulām
english: "Formerly occupied by the heroes of our ancestors, true to her name, with firm gates, filled with elephants, horses, and chariots —"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyair vaiśyaiḥ svakarmanirataiḥ sadā jitendriyair mahotsāhair vṛtāmātyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: "— surrounded always by brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas devoted to their own duties, with senses controlled, of great enterprise, and by thousands of ministers —"

sanskrit: prāsādair vividhākārair vṛtāṃ vaidyakanākulām kaccit samuditāṃ sphītām ayodhyāṃ parirakṣasi
english: "— encircled by palaces of varied forms, filled with physicians — do you protect Ayodhyā, prosperous and flourishing?"

sanskrit: kaccic caityaśatair juṣṭaḥ suniviṣṭanaranākulaḥ devasthānaiḥ prapābhiś ca taḍāgaiś copaśobhitaḥ
english: "Frequented by hundreds of sacred trees, thronged with well-settled inhabitants, adorned with shrines, drinking-halls, and tanks —"

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭanaranārīkaḥ samājotsavaśobhitaḥ sukṛṣṭasīmā paśumān hiṃsābhir abhivarjitaḥ
english: "— whose men and women are joyful, beautified by festivals and assemblies, with well-tilled fields, rich in cattle, and free from acts of violence —"

sanskrit: adevamātṛko ramyaḥ śvāpadaiḥ parivarjitaḥ kaccij janapadaḥ sphītaḥ sukhaṃ vasati rāghava
english: "— not dependent on rain alone for water, charming, free from beasts of prey — does your flourishing realm dwell in happiness, O Rāghava?"

sanskrit: kaccit te dayitāḥ sarve kṛṣigorakṣajīvinaḥ vārtāyāṃ saṃśritas tāta loko hi sukham edhate
english: "Are all those who live by farming and cattle-keeping dear to you? Dear boy, it is by the people's livelihood that prosperity grows."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ guptiparīhāraiḥ kaccit te bharaṇaṃ kṛtam rakṣyā hi rājñā dharmeṇa sarve viṣayavāsinaḥ
english: "Have you provided for their sustenance through measures of protection and relief? For all who dwell in the realm must by dharma be protected by the king."

sanskrit: kaccit striyaḥ sāntvayasi kaccit tāś ca surakṣitāḥ kaccin na śraddadhāsyāsāṃ kaccid guhyaṃ na bhāṣase
english: "Do you conciliate women? Are they well guarded? Do you not trust them excessively? Do you not disclose secrets to them?"

sanskrit: kaccin nāgavanaṃ guptaṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca tṛpyasi kaccid darśayase nityaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vibhūṣitam utthāyotthāya pūrvāhṇe rājaputro mahāpathe
english: "Is the elephant forest protected, and do you ensure the elephants are satisfied? Do you show yourself daily adorned to the people, rising early each morning on the royal highway?"

sanskrit: kaccit sarvāṇi durgāṇi dhanadhānyāyudhodakaiḥ yantraiś ca paripūrṇāni tathā śilpidhanurdharaiḥ
english: "Are all your fortresses filled with wealth, grain, weapons, water, engines of war, and also with craftsmen and archers?"

sanskrit: āyas te vipulaḥ kaccit kaccid alpataro vyayaḥ apātreṣu na te kaccit kośo gacchati rāghava
english: "Is your income large and your expenditure smaller? Does your treasury not go to those unworthy of it, O Rāghava?"

sanskrit: devatārthe ca pitrarthe brāhmaṇābhyāgateṣu ca yodheṣu mitravargeṣu kaccid gacchati te vyayaḥ
english: "Does your expenditure go toward the purposes of the gods, of the ancestors, toward brāhmaṇas and guests, toward warriors, and toward the company of friends?"

sanskrit: kaccid āryo viśuddhātmā kṣāritaś corakarmaṇā apṛṣṭaḥ śāstrakuśalair na lobhād badhyate śuciḥ
english: "Does a noble, pure-souled man, falsely accused of theft, go unquestioned by those skilled in the śāstras and remain unbound out of greed — remaining spotless?"

sanskrit: gṛhītaś caiva pṛṣṭaś ca kāle dṛṣṭaḥ sakāraṇaḥ kaccin na mucyate coro dhanalobhān nararṣabha
english: "When a thief is caught, questioned, and duly examined in due course with cause established — is he not released out of greed for money, O bull among men?"

sanskrit: vyasane kaccid āḍhyasya dugatasya ca rāghava arthaṃ virāgāḥ paśyanti tavāmātyās bahuśrutāḥ
english: "In a case of calamity affecting alike the wealthy and the destitute, O Rāghava, do your widely-learned ministers decide the matter without partiality?"

sanskrit: yāni mithyābhiśastānāṃ patanty asrāṇi rāghava tāni putrapaśūn ghnanti prītyartham anuśāsataḥ
english: "The tears that fall from those falsely accused, O Rāghava, they destroy the sons and cattle of him who punishes out of partiality."

sanskrit: kaccid vṛdhāṃś ca bālāṃś ca vaidyamukhyāṃś ca rāghava dānena manasā vācā tribhir etair bubhūṣase
english: "Do you cherish the elderly, children, and chief physicians, O Rāghava, by these three means — gifts, thought, and word?"

sanskrit: kaccid gurūṃś ca vṛddhāṃś ca tāpasān devatātithīn caityāṃś ca sarvān siddhārthān brāhmaṇāṃś ca namasyasi
english: "Do you pay homage to teachers, elders, ascetics, guests of the gods, all sacred shrines, and the accomplished brāhmaṇas?"

sanskrit: kaccid arthena vā dharmaṃ dharmaṃ dharmeṇa vā punaḥ ubhau vā prītilobhena kāmena na vibādhase
english: "Do you not obstruct dharma by means of wealth, nor wealth by means of dharma, nor both of them by pleasure born of desire and passion?"

sanskrit: kaccid arthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca jayatāṃ vara vibhajya kāle kālajña sarvān bharata sevase
english: "Having apportioned wealth, dharma, and pleasure each to its proper time, do you attend to all three, O Bharata, best of the victorious, you who know the right time?"

sanskrit: kaccit te brāhmaṇāḥ śarma sarvaśāstrārthakovidāḥ āśaṃsante mahāprājña paurajānapadaiḥ saha
english: "Do the brāhmaṇas who are versed in all the meanings of the śāstras wish you well, O greatly wise one, together with the citizens and the people of the realm?"

sanskrit: nāstikyam anṛtaṃ krodhaṃ pramādaṃ dīrghasūtratām adarśanaṃ jñānavatām ālasyaṃ pañcavṛttitām
english: "Impiety, falsehood, anger, negligence, procrastination, avoidance of those with wisdom, laziness, indulgence in the five sensory addictions —"

sanskrit: ekacintanam arthānām anarthajñaiś ca mantraṇam niścitānām anārambhaṃ mantrasyāparilakṣaṇam
english: "— deliberating on affairs alone, taking counsel with those ignorant of consequences, failure to begin what has been resolved, and failure to guard secret counsel —"

sanskrit: maṅgalasyāprayogaṃ ca pratyutthānaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ kaccit tvaṃ varjayasy etān rājadoṣāṃś caturdaśa
english: "— neglect of auspicious rites, and failure to rise in greeting on all occasions — do you shun these fourteen faults of kings?"

sanskrit: kaccit svādukṛtaṃ bhojyam eko nāśnāsi rāghava kaccid āśaṃsamānebhyo mitrebhyaḥ saṃprayacchasi
english: "Do you not eat food prepared with fine flavours alone by yourself, O Rāghava? Do you give a share to your friends who are deserving?"

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha kiṃ me dharmād vihīnasya rājadharmaḥ kariṣyati
english: Having heard Rāma's words, Bharata replied: "What shall the dharma of kingship do for me who am bereft of dharma?"

sanskrit: śāśvato 'yaṃ sadā dharmaḥ sthito 'smāsu nararṣabha jyeṣṭha putre sthite rājan na kanīyān bhaven nṛpaḥ
english: "This is the eternal dharma ever established among us, O bull among men: while the eldest son lives, O king, a younger son cannot become king."

sanskrit: sa samṛddhāṃ mayā sārdham ayodhyāṃ gaccha rāghava abhiṣecaya cātmānaṃ kulasyāsya bhavāya naḥ
english: "Come back to Ayodhyā in her prosperity together with me, O Rāghava, and consecrate yourself as king for the welfare of this dynasty."

sanskrit: rājānaṃ mānuṣaṃ prāhur devatve saṃmato mama yasya dharmārthasahitaṃ vṛttam āhur amānuṣam
english: "They call a king human, yet in my estimation he is regarded as divine — he whose conduct is conjoined with dharma and artha is said to be more than human."

sanskrit: kekayasthe ca mayi tu tvayi cāraṇyam āśrite divam ārya gato rājā yāyajūkaḥ satāṃ mataḥ
english: "While I was in the Kekaya country and you had resorted to the forest, the king — that sacrificer, honoured by the righteous — departed to heaven, O noble one."

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha puruṣavyāghra kriyatām udakaṃ pituḥ ahaṃ cāyaṃ ca śatrughnaḥ pūrvam eva kṛtodakau
english: "Rise up, O tiger among men; let the water-offering be made to father. Śatrughna and I have already performed ours."

sanskrit: priyeṇa kila dattaṃ hi pitṛlokeṣu rāghava akṣayyaṃ bhavatīty āhur bhavāṃś caiva pituḥ priyaḥ
english: "That which is given by one who is beloved is said to be inexhaustible in the world of the ancestors, O Rāghava, and you indeed are beloved of your father."

sanskrit: tāṃ śrutvā karuṇāṃ vācaṃ pitur maraṇasaṃhitām rāghavo bharatenoktāṃ babhūva gatacetanaḥ
english: Hearing those piteous words spoken by Bharata that were connected with his father's death, the Rāghava lost consciousness.

sanskrit: vāgvajraṃ bharatenoktam amanojñaṃ paraṃtapaḥ pragṛhya bāhū rāmo vai puṣpitāgro yathā drumaḥ vane paraśunā kṛttas tathā bhuvi papāta ha
english: Struck by the thunderbolt of those unwelcome words spoken by Bharata, that scorcher of foes Rāma threw up both his arms and fell to the ground like a tree in full bloom felled in the forest by an axe.

sanskrit: tathā hi patitaṃ rāmaṃ jagatyāṃ jagatīpatim kūlaghātapariśrāntaṃ prasuptam iva kuñjaram
english: So Rāma, lord of the earth, lay fallen on the ground, like an elephant exhausted by the battering of a riverbank and lying asleep.

sanskrit: bhrātaras te maheṣvāsaṃ sarvataḥ śokakarśitam rudantaḥ saha vaidehyā siṣicuḥ salilena vai
english: His brothers, weeping, together with the Vaidehī, sprinkled water on that great bowman who was worn thin by grief on every side.

sanskrit: sa tu saṃjñāṃ punar labdhvā netrābhyām āsram utsṛjan upākrāmata kākutsthaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ bahubhāṣitum
english: Regaining consciousness, shedding tears from both his eyes, the Kākutstha began to speak piteously at length.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tasya mayā kāryaṃ durjātena mahātmanā yo mṛto mama śokena na mayā cāpi saṃskṛtaḥ
english: "What now is to be done for that great-souled man by me, ill-born as I am, who died of grief for me and was not even cremated by me?"

sanskrit: aho bharata siddhārtho yena rājā tvayānagha śatrugheṇa ca sarveṣu pretakṛtyeṣu satkṛtaḥ
english: "Ah, Bharata has achieved his purpose — the king was honoured by you, O sinless one, and by Śatrughna in all the funerary rites."

sanskrit: niṣpradhānām anekāgraṃ narendreṇa vinākṛtām nivṛttavanavāso 'pi nāyodhyāṃ gantum utsahe
english: "Even though my forest-dwelling is over, I cannot bring myself to go to Ayodhyā — bereft of its sovereign, leaderless, scattered in attention."

sanskrit: samāptavanavāsaṃ mām ayodhyāyāṃ paraṃtapa ko nu śāsiṣyati punas tāte lokāntaraṃ gate
english: "When my period of forest-dwelling is over, O scorcher of foes, who will govern me again in Ayodhyā, now that father has gone to another world?"

sanskrit: purā prekṣya suvṛttaṃ māṃ pitā yāny āha sāntvayan vākyāni tāni śroṣyāmi kutaḥ karṇasukhāny aham
english: "Those comforting words which father used to speak to me long ago, seeing my good conduct — whence shall I hear those words, so pleasing to the ear?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa bharataṃ bhāryām abhyetya rāghavaḥ uvāca śokasaṃtaptaḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
english: Having spoken thus to Bharata, the Rāghava, scorched by grief, approached his wife whose face resembled the full moon and spoke to her.

sanskrit: sīte mṛtas te śvaśuraḥ pitrā hīno 'si lakṣmaṇa bharato duḥkham ācaṣṭe svargataṃ pṛthivīpatim
english: "Sītā, your father-in-law is dead. You are bereft of your father, Lakṣmaṇa. Bharata brings word of sorrow: the lord of the earth has gone to heaven."

sanskrit: sāntvayitvā tu tāṃ rāmo rudantīṃ janakātmajām uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ tatra duḥkhito duḥkhitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having consoled Sītā, daughter of Janaka, who was weeping, Rāma — himself afflicted with grief — spoke these words of sorrow to Lakṣmaṇa there.

sanskrit: ānayeṅgudipiṇyākaṃ cīram āhara cottaram bring jalakriyārthaṃ tātasya gamiṣyāmi mahātmanaḥ
english: "Bring the piṇyāka paste of iṅgudi fruit, and fetch an upper garment of bark-cloth; for the sake of the water-offering for our great-souled father, I shall go."

sanskrit: sītā purastād vrajatu tvam enām abhito vraja ahaṃ paścād gamiṣyāmi gatir hy eṣā sudāruṇā
english: "Let Sītā go ahead; you follow closely beside her; I shall go last — for this path is most terrible."

sanskrit: tato nityānugas teṣāṃ viditātmā mahāmatiḥ mṛdur dāntaś ca śāntaś ca rāme ca dṛḍha bhaktimān
english: Then Suman­tra, their constant companion who had known their souls, who was of great wisdom, gentle, self-controlled, tranquil, and of firm devotion to Rāma —

sanskrit: sumantras tair nṛpasutaiḥ sārdham āśvāsya rāghavam avātārayad ālambya nadīṃ mandākinīṃ śivām
english: — Sumantra, together with those princes, having comforted Rāghava, led him down, supporting him, to the auspicious river Mandākinī.

sanskrit: te sutīrthāṃ tataḥ kṛcchrād upāgamya yaśasvinaḥ nadīṃ mandākinīṃ ramyāṃ sadā puṣpitakānanām
english: Those glorious ones then, with difficulty, approached the Mandākinī, beautiful river always attended by flowering groves, at a good ford.

sanskrit: śīghrasrotasam āsādya tīrthaṃ śivam akardamam siṣicus tūdakaṃ rājñe tata etad bhavatv iti
english: Having reached its swift current at an auspicious and unmuddied ford, they offered the water to the king, saying, "Let this be for him."

sanskrit: pragṛhya ca mahīpālo jalapūritam añjalim diśaṃ yāmyām abhimukho rudan vacanam abravīt
english: The lord of the earth, cupping his hands filled with water, facing toward the south, weeping, spoke these words:

sanskrit: etat te rājaśārdūla vimalaṃ toyam akṣayam pitṛlokagatasyādya maddattaṃ upatiṣṭhatu
english: "O tiger among kings, may this pure, inexhaustible water, given by me today, reach you who have gone to the world of the ancestors."

sanskrit: tato mandākinī tīrāt pratyuttīrya sa rāghavaḥ pituś cakāra tejasvī nivāpaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Then the glorious Rāghava, ascending from the bank of the Mandākinī, performed together with his brothers the oblation of food for his father.

sanskrit: aiṅgudaṃ badarīmiśraṃ piṇyākaṃ darbhasaṃstare nyasya rāmaḥ suduḥkhārto rudan vacanam abravīt
english: Rāma, deeply afflicted with grief, placed the piṇyāka paste mixed with jujube and iṅgudi upon a spread of darbha grass, and weeping, spoke these words:

sanskrit: idaṃ bhuṅkṣva mahārājaprīto yad aśanā vayam yadannaḥ puruṣo bhavati tadannās tasya devatāḥ
english: "Eat this with pleasure, O great king — for what we eat is what we offer. Whatever food a man eats, his deities receive that same food."

sanskrit: tatas tenaiva mārgeṇa pratyuttīrya nadītaṭāt āruroha naravyāghro ramyasānuṃ mahīdharam
english: Then by the same path, ascending from the riverbank, that tiger among men climbed the lovely ridge of the mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ parṇakuṭīdvāram āsādya jagatīpatiḥ parijagrāha pāṇibhyām ubhau bharatalakṣmaṇau
english: Then the lord of the earth, reaching the doorway of the leaf-hut, took both Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa by the hands.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu rudatāṃ śabdāt pratiśrutkābhavad girau bhrātṝṇāṃ saha vaidehyā siṃhānāṃ nardatām iva
english: From the sound of those brothers weeping together with the Vaidehī, an echo arose on the mountain, like the roaring of lions.

sanskrit: vijñāya tumulaṃ śabdaṃ trastā bharatasainikāḥ abruvaṃś cāpi rāmeṇa bharataḥ saṃgato dhruvam teṣām eva mahāñ śabdaḥ śocatāṃ pitaraṃ mṛtam
english: Understanding the tumultuous sound, Bharata's soldiers were startled and said: "Surely Bharata has met with Rāma" — for that great sound was of those very men lamenting their dead father.

sanskrit: atha vāsān parityajya taṃ sarve 'bhimukhāḥ svanam apy eka manaso jagmur yathāsthānaṃ pradhāvitāḥ
english: Then, abandoning their encampments, all of them with one mind rushed toward that sound, running as fast as their places allowed.

sanskrit: hayair anye gajair anye rathair anye svalaṃkṛtaiḥ sukumārās tathaivānye padbhir eva narā yayuḥ
english: Some went on horses, some on elephants, some on well-adorned chariots; others, the tender-limbed, went on foot alone.

sanskrit: aciraproṣitaṃ rāmaṃ ciraviproṣitaṃ yathā draṣṭukāmo janaḥ sarvo jagāma sahasāśramam
english: All the people, desiring to see Rāma — though he had been away only briefly, as if he had been long absent — rushed at once to the hermitage.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇāṃ tvaritās te tu draṣṭukāmāḥ samāgamam yayur bahuvidhair yānaiḥ khuranemisamākulaiḥ
english: Hastening eagerly to witness the brothers' reunion, they went in vehicles of every kind, crowded with the sounds of hooves and wheels.

sanskrit: sā bhūmir bahubhir yānaiḥ khuranemisamāhatā mumoca tumulaṃ śabdaṃ dyaur ivābhrasamāgame
english: The earth, struck by the many vehicles with their hooves and wheels, gave forth a tumultuous sound, like the sky at the gathering of clouds.

sanskrit: tena vitrāsitā nāgāḥ kareṇuparivāritāḥ āvāsayanto gandhena jagmur anyad vanaṃ tataḥ
english: Frightened by that sound, the elephants surrounded by their females, marking the air with their scent, departed to another forest.

sanskrit: varāhamṛgasiṃhāś ca mahiṣāḥ sarkṣavānarāḥ vyāghra gokarṇagavayā vitreṣuḥ pṛṣataiḥ saha
english: Wild boars, deer, lions, buffaloes, bears and monkeys, tigers, elk, and gayal — all were frightened, along with spotted deer.

sanskrit: rathāṅgasāhvā natyūhā haṃsāḥ kāraṇḍavāḥ plavāḥ tathā puṃskokilāḥ krauñcā visaṃjñā bhejire diśaḥ
english: Cakravāka birds, water-cocks, geese, kāraṇḍava ducks, grebes, male cuckoos, and herons — bewildered — fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastair ākāśaṃ pakṣibhir vṛtam manuṣyair āvṛtā bhūmir ubhayaṃ prababhau tadā
english: The sky filled with birds frightened by that sound; the earth was covered with human beings — both gleamed brilliantly at that time.

sanskrit: tān narān bāṣpapūrṇākṣān samīkṣyātha suduḥkhitān paryaṣvajata dharmajñaḥ pitṛvan mātṛvac ca saḥ
english: Beholding those men with eyes full of tears and deeply afflicted, he who knew dharma embraced them like a father and like a mother.

sanskrit: sa tatra kāṃś cit pariṣasvaje narān narāś ca ke cit tu tam abhyavādayan cakāra sarvān savayasyabāndhavān yathārham āsādya tadā nṛpātmajaḥ
english: There he embraced some men, and some men greeted him in return; then that prince, having duly met all of them together with their companions and kinsmen, honoured them each according to their desert.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa teṣāṃ rudatāṃ mahātmanāṃ bhuvaṃ ca khaṃ cānuvinādayan svanaḥ guhā girīṇāṃ ca diśaś ca saṃtataṃ mṛdaṅgaghoṣapratimo viśuśruve
english: Then the sound of those great souls weeping, reverberating across the earth and through the sky, filling the caves of the mountains and all directions, was heard continually like the roar of a kettle drum.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaḥ purataḥ kṛtvā dārān daśarathasya ca abhicakrāma taṃ deśaṃ rāmadarśanatarṣitaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha, placing the wives of Daśaratha before him, advanced toward that place, thirsting for the sight of Rāma.

sanskrit: rājapatnyaś ca gacchantyo mandaṃ mandākinīṃ prati dadṛśus tatra tat tīrthaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇasevitam
english: The royal wives, going slowly toward the Mandākinī, saw there that ford which had been frequented by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: kausalyā bāṣpapūrṇena mukhena pariśuṣyatā sumitrām abravīd dīnā yāś cānyā rājayoṣitaḥ
english: Kausalyā, her face withered and filled with tears, spoke pitiably to Sumitrā and to the other royal women:

sanskrit: idaṃ teṣām anāthānāṃ kliṣṭam akliṣṭa karmaṇām vane prāk kevalaṃ tīrthaṃ ye te nirviṣayī kṛtāḥ
english: "This is the only ford in the forest — the one bathing place — of those who, though untiring in their deeds, are now left without a lord, stripped of their kingdom."

sanskrit: itaḥ sumitre putras te sadā jalam atandritaḥ svayaṃ harati saumitrir mama putrasya kāraṇāt
english: "From here, O Sumitrā, your son the son of Sumitrā — tireless — always fetches water himself for the sake of my son."

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu sā dadarśa mahītale pitur iṅgudipiṇyākaṃ nyastam āyatalocanā
english: The wide-eyed queen saw on the ground, on darbha grass with tips pointing south, the piṇyāka paste of iṅgudi placed there as an offering to his father.

sanskrit: taṃ bhūmau pitur ārtena nyastaṃ rāmeṇa vīkṣya sā uvāca devī kausalyā sarvā daśarathastriyaḥ
english: Beholding that offering placed on the ground in grief for his father by Rāma, Queen Kausalyā spoke to all the wives of Daśaratha:

sanskrit: idam ikṣvākunāthasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ rāghaveṇa pitur dattaṃ paśyataitad yathāvidhi
english: "Behold — this is what has been duly given by the Rāghava to his father: the offering of the great-souled Rāghava, lord of the Ikṣvākus."

sanskrit: tasya devasamānasya pārthivasya mahātmanaḥ naitad aupayikaṃ manye bhuktabhogasya bhojanam
english: "For that great-souled king who was equal to the gods, who had enjoyed every pleasure — this, I think, is not a fitting meal."

sanskrit: caturantāṃ mahīṃ bhuktvā mahendra sadṛśo bhuvi katham iṅgudipiṇyākaṃ sa bhuṅkte vasudhādhipaḥ
english: "He who ruled the earth bounded by four seas, who was like Mahendra on earth — how is it that that lord of the earth now subsists on iṅgudi paste?"

sanskrit: ato duḥkhataraṃ loke na kiṃ cit pratibhāti mā yatra rāmaḥ pitur dadyād iṅgudīkṣodam ṛddhimān
english: "Nothing in the world appears more sorrowful to me than this — that prosperous Rāma should offer his father nothing but the expressed juice of iṅgudi."

sanskrit: rāmeṇeṅgudipiṇyākaṃ pitur dattaṃ samīkṣya me kathaṃ duḥkhena hṛdayaṃ na sphoṭati sahasradhā
english: "Having seen the iṅgudi paste given by Rāma as an offering to his father, how does my heart not burst into a thousand pieces from grief?"

sanskrit: evam ārtāṃ sapatnyas tā jagmur āśvāsya tāṃ tadā dadṛśuś cāśrame rāmaṃ svargāc cyutam ivāmaram
english: Her co-wives then consoled her in her distress and went on, and they saw Rāma in the hermitage — like an immortal fallen from heaven.

sanskrit: sarvabhogaiḥ parityaktaṃ rāma saṃprekṣya mātaraḥ ārtā mumucur aśrūṇi sasvaraṃ śokakarśitāḥ
english: Beholding Rāma abandoned by every luxury, the mothers, afflicted and worn thin by grief, shed tears with audible weeping.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ rāmaḥ samutthāya jagrāha caraṇāñ śubhān mātṝṇāṃ manujavyāghraḥ sarvāsāṃ satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: Rāma, that tiger among men, of firm vows, rose and clasped the auspicious feet of all those mothers.

sanskrit: tāḥ pāṇibhiḥ sukhasparśair mṛdvaṅgulitalaiḥ śubhaiḥ pramamārjū rajaḥ pṛṣṭhād rāmasyāyatalocanāḥ
english: With their soft-touching, gentle-fingered, auspicious hands, those wide-eyed women wiped the dust from Rāma's back.

sanskrit: saumitrir api tāḥ sarvā mātṝḥ saṃprekṣya duḥkhitaḥ abhyavādayatāsaktaṃ śanai rāmād anantaram
english: The son of Sumitrā too, gazing upon all those mothers with distress, greeted them devoutly and gently, following right after Rāma.

sanskrit: yathā rāme tathā tasmin sarvā vavṛtire striyaḥ vṛttiṃ daśarathāj jāte lakṣmaṇe śubhalakṣaṇe
english: Just as they had behaved toward Rāma, so all the women conducted themselves toward him — toward Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks, born of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: sītāpi caraṇāṃs tāsām upasaṃgṛhya duḥkhitā śvaśrūṇām aśrupūrṇākṣī sā babhūvāgrataḥ sthitā
english: Sītā too, grief-stricken, clasped the feet of those mothers-in-law, her eyes filled with tears, and stood before them.

sanskrit: tāṃ pariṣvajya duḥkhārtāṃ mātā duhitaraṃ yathā vanavāsakṛśāṃ dīnāṃ kausalyā vākyam abravīt
english: Embracing her who was afflicted with grief, as a mother would embrace a daughter, Kausalyā spoke to the emaciated, forlorn Sītā grown thin by forest-dwelling:

sanskrit: videharājasya sutā snuṣā daśarathasya ca rāmapatnī kathaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃprāptā nirjane vane
english: "Daughter of the king of Videha, daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, wife of Rāma — how have you come to suffer so in this solitary forest?"

sanskrit: padmam ātapasaṃtaptaṃ parikliṣṭam ivotpalam kāñcanaṃ rajasā dhvastaṃ kliṣṭaṃ candram ivāmbudaiḥ
english: "Like a lotus scorched by the sun's heat, like a blue lotus withered, like gold obscured by dust, like the moon afflicted by clouds —"

sanskrit: mukhaṃ te prekṣya māṃ śoko dahaty agnir ivāśrayam bhṛśaṃ manasi vaidehi vyasanāraṇisaṃbhavaḥ
english: "— beholding your face, O Vaidehī, grief burns me like fire consuming a dry abode, blazing fiercely in my heart, born from the kindling-sticks of calamity."

sanskrit: bruvantyām evam ārtāyāṃ jananyāṃ bharatāgrajaḥ pādāv āsādya jagrāha vasiṣṭhasya sa rāghavaḥ
english: While his mother spoke thus in her distress, the elder brother of Bharata, the Rāghava, approached and clasped the feet of Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: purohitasyāgnisamasya tasya vai bṛhaspater indra ivāmarādhipaḥ pragṛhya pādau susamṛddhatejasaḥ sahaiva tenopaviveśa rāghavaḥ
english: Of that family priest who was equal to fire, that Bṛhaspati — grasping the feet of him whose splendour was fully ripened — the Rāghava sat down together with him, as Indra the lord of immortals would sit with Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: tato jaghanyaṃ sahitaiḥ sa mantribhiḥ purapradhānaiś ca sahaiva sainikaiḥ janena dharmajñatamena dharmavān upopaviṣṭo bharatas tadāgrajam
english: Then righteous Bharata sat down behind, together with ministers, the foremost men of the city, soldiers, and the people who were most knowing in dharma, in the presence of his elder brother.

sanskrit: upopaviṣṭas tu tadā sa vīryavāṃs tapasviveṣeṇa samīkṣya rāghavam śriyā jvalantaṃ bharataḥ kṛtāñjalir yathā mahendraḥ prayataḥ prajāpatim
english: Having sat down, that valiant Bharata gazed at the Rāghava blazing with splendour even in his ascetic garb, and with hands folded in reverence — as Mahendra, purified, regards Prajāpati.

sanskrit: kim eṣa vākyaṃ bharato 'dya rāghavaṃ praṇamya satkṛtya ca sādhu vakṣyati itīva tasyāryajanasya tattvato babhūva kautūhalam uttamaṃ tadā
english: "What words will Bharata speak today to the Rāghava, having bowed to him and duly honoured him?" — such, in truth, was the keen and supreme curiosity of all the noble people gathered there at that moment.

sanskrit: sa rāghavaḥ satyadhṛtiś ca lakṣmaṇo mahānubhāvo bharataś ca dhārmikaḥ vṛtāḥ suhṛdbhiś ca virejur adhvare yathā sadasyaiḥ sahitās trayo 'gnayaḥ
english: Rāma the Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa steadfast in truth, great-souled, and righteous Bharata — surrounded by their friends — shone like the three sacrificial fires accompanied by their priests at a Vedic rite.
